synopsis: The Dry Ferry, day thirteen. The Tamm Line comes onto the only rock between the rims with a hundred and sixty-nine gallons standing and seventeen dry days ahead of it, and finds the Assembly's shutter open above the depot: Oreth Vask has ridden two hundred and fifty miles on four hask and no wagon and has been waiting three days. He has known a month, by way of Thecla Bram, who has a correspondence and a debtor. He buys their water down from thirty-one blocks to eleven with one word to the depot, says it is not part of anything he is going to say to them, and means it. Then he asks Denet Rasca how deep, and writes the answer down, and stops writing. The offer is five numbered terms and it would save every person on the Line, and the fifth term names Pell Corrow's daughter. That night eleven people argue it out under an awning tied to mooring rings that once held ships -- six for taking it, three for carrying the surveyor on, two who will not say -- and Sabra Onn, whose whole trade dies if the water is real, says dig it at the Centre in front of the joint tile. Ysoly reads them the Fourth Article instead: dig it and you make water standing within the bounds, half a mile from the only Warden of the Third Rank between the rims. At first light Denet says yes and asks for four lines on the College roll, which is the one thing that cannot be bought, and the sale dies on a clerical point. Vask writes two letters, finishes one sentence, and does not finish the other. The Line rolls south at second light with eight hundred and fifty gallons, eleven blocks cut on the debt face, twenty that have no face at all, and a man in the fourth wagon's shadow that nobody speaks to.
title: What the Assembly Knows
